preamble: Middle Chinese voiced velar [g] (the 群 initial) before the front vowels and glides [i, y] surfaces as voiceless unaspirated [tɕ] in several Sinitic branches, combining devoicing with velar palatalization. In Mandarin this outcome is limited to the oblique (non-level) tones, while level-tone syllables became aspirated [tɕʰ]; in New Xiang (Changsha), where the voiced obstruents became voiceless unaspirated across the board, level-tone words also show [tɕ].

examples.note: Oblique-tone voiced initial devoiced to unaspirated [k] and palatalized to [tɕ] before the front medial.
New Xiang devoiced the Middle Chinese voiced obstruents to unaspirated stops in all tones, so level-tone 琴 has [tɕ], unlike Mandarin qín [tɕʰ].

period: Middle Chinese to modern varieties (c. 600 CE onward)
